concept.title: Harmonic Measure on the Berggren Tree Boundary — Random Walks and the 3-adic Cantor Set
concept.concept_description:
**Domain**: Pythagorean <-> Probability

**Hypothesis**: The boundary of the Berggren ternary tree of primitive Pythagorean triples is a 3-adic Cantor set, and a random walk on the tree (choosing among the three Berggren moves with probabilities p₁,p₂,p₃) converges to a harmonic measure on this boundary whose dimension and entropy are exactly computable. The conjecture: the harmonic measure of the random walk is a Bernoulli measure on the 3-adic boundary with entropy equal to the Shannon entropy H(p₁,p₂,p₃), and the spectral gap of the walk (the second eigenvalue of the associated Markov operator on the tree) is governed by the silver ratio log(1+√2) structure of the tree's growth.

**Test**: Formalize the boundary of the Berggren tree as the set of infinite words over the 3-letter alphabet {A,B,C}, i.e., the 3-adic Cantor set. Define the random walk with transition probabilities (p₁,p₂,p₃). Prove the harmonic measure is the product Bernoulli measure, compute its entropy and Hausdorff dimension, and compute the spectral gap of the Markov operator. Relate the return probabilities to the silver-ratio growth exponent already proven for the tree.

**Why now**: The catalog has exact metric growth (silver speed limit), the groupoid structure, and the hyperbolic embedding — but no probabilistic/ergodic theory. Random walks on the Berggren tree are a natural, untouched probabilistic counterpart to the deterministic geometry, connecting to the theory of random walks on hyperbolic groups, harmonic measure, and the geometry of Cantor-set boundaries.

**If true**: The Berggren tree becomes a fully understood example in the theory of random walks on hyperbolic trees — with exact harmonic measure, entropy, and spectral gap — a clean probabilistic companion to its deterministic geometry, with connections to the theory of free groups and their boundaries.

**If false**: The harmonic measure fails to be Bernoulli (e.g., the boundary carries a non-product measure), which would reveal hidden structure in how the three moves distribute mass, itself a novel statement.

# Future directions

The thread opened with two questions — the finite-key probability formula and
crossing-probability monotonicity — both of which are proved in
`Catalog/Combinatorics/BernoulliThresholdCoupling.lean`.  Since then the work has
gone into *depth*: a sprinkling/thinning calculus, the Bollobás–Thomason
threshold window, site-dependent densities with the Margulis–Russo formula, a
Poincaré (variance–influence) inequality proved by hybrid paths, its integrated
odds-ratio form, a matching *reverse* Poincaré inequality with the two-sided
Russo differential inequality, and a self-contained `p`-biased Fourier analysis
on the discrete cube.

This cycle completed that Fourier development and used it to convert two of the
inequalities into exact identities:

* `Catalog/Combinatorics/BernoulliFourierParseval.lean` — the product rule for
  the biased expectation, full orthogonality of the characters `ψ_S`, the
  reproducing-kernel identity, **completeness** of the biased Fourier basis
  (`fourier_expansion`), **Parseval** (`parseval`), the biased Plancherel
  identity for Boolean functions (`fourier_weight_sum`), and the exact energy
  decomposition `4P(1-P) = 4p(1-p) ∑_v I_v² + (level ≥ 2 energy)`, which exhibits
  the `ℓ²` influence bound as the statement that a remainder is nonnegative and
  pins down its equality case.
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/BernoulliPoincareDefect.lean` — the identity
  `∑_{S ∋ v} (p(1-p))^{|S|} \hat f(S)² = p(1-p) E[(D_v f)²]` (the biased form of
  `Inf_v(f) = ∑_{S ∋ v} \hat f(S)²`), the resulting Efron–Stein/Poincaré
  inequality **for arbitrary functions** together with its exact defect
  `∑_{S ≠ ∅} (|S| - 1)(p(1-p))^{|S|} \hat f(S)²`, and, for increasing events, the
  Fourier formula for the total influence, the Poincaré inequality with exact
  remainder, and its equality case (`poincare_eq_iff_degree_le_one`).

The following conjectures are the natural next targets; each is falsifiable at
the level of finite site sets, so each can be tested numerically — with the exact
rational harness of `ComputationalEvidence.md` — before being attacked formally.

## Conjecture 1 (two-point hypercontractivity and its tensorization)

For every `f : Bool → ℝ`, every `ρ ∈ [0,1]` with `ρ² ≤ p(1-p)/max(p,1-p)²`, and
the biased noise operator `T_ρ`, one has `‖T_ρ f‖_4 ≤ ‖f‖_2`; and the same
inequality holds for functions on `ι → Bool` with the same `ρ`, by tensorizing
along `expP_prod`.

*The key insight is* that `expP_prod` — proved in this cycle — is exactly the
statement that the biased measure is a product measure, and tensorization of a
hypercontractive estimate is nothing but repeated application of the product
rule coordinate by coordinate; the two-point case is a single two-variable
polynomial inequality accessible to `nlinarith` after clearing denominators.

*Why now?* Hypercontractivity is the only missing ingredient between the present
development and the whole KKL/Talagrand circle: the Fourier expansion, Parseval,
the level decomposition, and the influence identity are all formal already, and
each of them is used verbatim in the classical proof.

## Conjecture 2 (Talagrand's `L¹`–`L²` inequality on the cube)

There is an absolute constant `C > 0` such that for every increasing event `A` on
a finite site set `ι`, writing `I_v = bernProb (1/2) (pivotalSet A v)`,

`P (1 - P) ≤ C · ∑_v I_v / Real.log (Real.exp 1 / I_v)`

(with the convention that a site of zero influence contributes `0`).

*The key insight is* that the present `ℓ²` bound and the defect identity already
give the two extreme cases — the `ℓ²` sum controls the variance exactly, and the
`ℓ¹` sum controls it with the crude Cauchy–Schwarz loss — so Talagrand's
inequality is precisely the interpolation obtained by splitting the Fourier
expansion at the level `log(1/I_v)` and applying Conjecture 1 to the tail.

*Why now?* Talagrand's inequality implies the KKL influence bound
`max_v I_v ≥ c log|ι| / |ι|`, so proving it closes two conjectures of this thread
at once; and its extremal family (tribes) is finite and directly testable
against the rational harness.

## Conjecture 3 (sharp threshold for transitive events)

If the automorphism group of `A ⊆ (ι → Bool)` acts transitively on `ι`, then all
influences are equal, and consequently the width of the density window on which
`bernProb p A` moves from `ε` to `1 - ε` is at most `C(ε) / log |ι|`.

*The key insight is* that under transitivity the Poincaré defect identity forces
`|ι| · I = 4 p(1-p) ∑_v I_v ≥ 4 P(1-P)`, so a *lower* bound on the single common
influence of the KKL type immediately upgrades Russo's formula to a logarithmic
threshold window — the symmetry replaces the union bound entirely.

*Why now?* The equal-influence step is a two-line consequence of the formal
statement `siteEnergy_eq_influence`, since the site energies are manifestly
invariant under automorphisms; only the KKL lower bound (Conjecture 2) is
missing.

## Conjecture 4 (BK / van den Berg–Kesten inequality)

For increasing events `A`, `B` on a finite site set define disjoint occurrence
`A □ B = {η | ∃ S T : Finset ι, Disjoint S T ∧ 1_S ∈ A ∧ 1_T ∈ B ∧ S ∪ T ⊆ open η}`.
Then `bernProb p (A □ B) ≤ bernProb p A * bernProb p B`.

*The key insight is* that `sum_prod_pushforward` already provides the exact
mechanism that BK needs — a coordinatewise duplication of the alphabet from
`Bool` to `Bool × Bool` — so the van den Berg–Kesten induction can be phrased as
a sequence of pushforwards along `Bool × Bool → Bool` rather than as a
measure-theoretic coupling.

*Why now?* The pushforward lemma, the pivotal calculus and the one-coordinate
decomposition `fun_decomp` built in this cycle are exactly the ingredients that
the classical proof manipulates informally; with the thinning law
`bernProb_and_le` already formalized, BK is the last elementary correlation
inequality of percolation still missing from the catalog.

## Conjecture 5 (self-duality of bond crossings at density 1/2)

For bond percolation on the `n × (n+1)` grid, the probability at `p = 1/2` that
the two short sides are joined by an open path equals exactly `1/2`; hence
`thresholdDensity` of that crossing event at level `1/2` is exactly `1/2` for
every `n`.

*The key insight is* that the complement of a horizontal open crossing is a
vertical closed crossing of the dual rectangle, and the map `ω ↦ ωᶜ` is
weight-preserving at `p = 1/2` (`weight (1/2) η = 2 ^ -|ι|` for every `η`), so
the duality is a bijection between two events of equal weight rather than an
analytic statement.

*Why now?* The catalog already has `bondThresholdConfig`, the bond form of the
finite-key formula, and `thresholdDensity`; the missing ingredient is a purely
combinatorial planar-duality lemma between open horizontal paths and closed
vertical paths, which is finite and checkable by enumeration for `n ≤ 3`.

Prove the map is a tree isomorphism preserving the ternary branching, and transfer at least one structural theorem (e.g., the uniqueness of the growth spine, or the groupoid action) from the Berggren side to the Markoff side.

**Why now**: The Markoff uniqueness conjecture (that every Markoff triple is uniquely determined by its largest element) is a famous open problem.
